With a strong foundation in innovation and research, the Group continues to empower students across diverse disciplines while addressing the evolving needs of industry and society. `n `n `n `n `n About MIT Group MIT Group at a Glance`n MIT Group of Institutions, established under MAEER in 1983 , has grown into one of Maharashtra's leading educational ecosystems. `n We provide:`n `n `n Infrastructure 1,000 Acres+`n `n `n `n Institutes 72+ Institutes`n `n `n `n Students 50,000+ Students`n `n `n `n Faculty 4,000+ Educators`n `n `n `n Staff 6,000+ Members`n `n `n `n Universities WPU MIT World Peace University `n `n `n `n Universities (ADT) MIT Art, Design & Technology `n `n `n `n `n `n Timeline `n Our Journey of Excellence`n From a visionary beginning to a multi-disciplinary educational ecosystem`n `n Early Years (1980s)`n `n Foundation of MIT`n Maharashtra Institute of Technology (MIT), one of the first private engineering colleges in the state, was established—becoming the flagship institute of MIT Group. `n `n `n 1983`n `n Establishment of MAEER`n Maharashtra Academy of Engineering & Educational Research (MAEER) was established in Pune as a society and charitable trust, marking a significant step. `n `n `n 1998`n `n Global Recognition by UNESCO`n UNESCO established the Chair for Human Rights, Democracy, Peace and Tolerance at MIT, recognizing its contribution to value-based education. `n `n `n 2000s–2010s`n `n Expansion Across Maharashtra`n MIT Group expanded rapidly, establishing multiple institutes and campuses across the state, strengthening its presence in diverse educational domains. `n `n `n `n `n `n Guiding Principles `n Five Principles of Holistic Development`n MIT Group believes in nurturing not just academic ability, but the complete personality of every student. Its education model is built on 5 core principles: `n `n Spirit of Inquiry`n To develop curiosity and encourage academic excellence.`n 01`n `n `n Discipline and Character`n To inculcate responsibility, integrity, and strong personal values.`n 02`n `n `n Social Commitment`n To inspire students to contribute meaningfully to society.`n 03`n `n `n Culture of Peace`n To promote harmony, tolerance, and universal understanding.`n 04`n `n `n Industry–Institute Interface`n To build strong connections between education and the professional world. `n 05`n `n `n `n `n `n About the Educational Philosophy `n From Darkness to Knowledge`n In Sanskrit, "Gu" means darkness and "Ru" means the light of knowledge. A Guru is one who leads students from ignorance to wisdom, not only shaping individual lives but also serving society at large. `n This philosophy reflects MIT Group's deep commitment to value-based education, teacher development, and nation-building. The Group continues to prepare educators and learners who can become knowledge leaders and value educators. `n `n `n `n `n `n `n `n `n Why It Stands Out Education with Scale, Purpose, and Impact`n MIT Group has grown into a powerful educational network with a strong footprint across Maharashtra. Its strength lies in: `n `n `n Wide academic diversity `n `n Experienced faculty `n `n Strong infrastructure `n `n Research and innovation focus `n `n Value-driven learning `n `n Strong social and industry connection `n `n This broad ecosystem enables MIT Group to respond to changing educational needs while staying rooted in its founding mission. `n `n `n `n

Karad’s journey is a story of vision, dedication, and transformation.`n Driven by the belief in value-based education , he has shaped MIT Group into a hub of excellence—nurturing engineers, scientists, and professionals who are not only skilled but also socially responsible.`n Inspired by Swami Vivekananda , his philosophy blends Science and Spirituality , aiming to create individuals who are: `n 01 Physically strong`n 02 Mentally alert`n 03 Intellectually sharp`n 04 Spiritually aware`n `n Educational Vision & Philosophy`n His initiatives reflect a deep commitment to society and culture`n World Peace Prayer practiced daily across campuses`n Spiritual & wellness initiatives for holistic growth`n National & International Robocon events promoting innovation`n World Peace Eco Park promoting sustainability`n Cultural & heritage initiatives rooted in Indian traditions`n A Vision for the Future`n With a mission to transform education and society, his leadership continues to guide MIT Group towards global excellence while nurturing responsible citizens and future leaders.`n `n `n `n `n `n Personal Background`n A village-born youngster went on to become an engineering professor and further created a world-class educational conglomerate that is transforming the lives of thousands through teaching methods rooted in India’s holistic thought. Approved by AICTE, New Delhi & Recognised by Government of Maharashtra & DTE Mumbai. `n `n `n Does the college provide experienced faculty? `n Yes, MITCORER has qualified and experienced faculty members with strong academic and research backgrounds. `n `n `n Are laboratories and practical facilities available? `n Yes, well-equipped laboratories are available for all departments. `n `n `n Does the college support research and innovation? `n Yes, the institute encourages research, projects, and innovation activities. `n `n `n What is Railway Engineering? `n Railway Engineering focuses on railway infrastructure, track design, signaling systems, and transportation engineering. `n `n `n What career opportunities are available in Railway Engineering? `n Students can work in Indian Railways, metro projects, infrastructure companies, and transportation sectors. `n `n `n Does MITCORER provide practical exposure in railway-related fields? `n Yes, the institute emphasizes industry-oriented learning and practical training. `n `n `n Does MITCORER provide placement assistance? `n Yes, a dedicated Training & Placement Cell supports students with placements and training. `n `n `n `n What is the highest placement package? `n The highest package has reached up to 21 LPA. `n `n `n Which companies visit the campus? `n Top IT, core engineering, and infrastructure companies visit for recruitment. `n `n `n Are internships provided? `n Yes, internship opportunities are provided as part of academic training. `n `n `n Does the college have a library? `n Yes, the college has a well-equipped library with digital resources and journals. `n `n `n Are hostel facilities available? `n Yes, the institute provides well-maintained separate hostel facilities for boys and girls. The hostels are equipped with essential amenities such as RO drinking water, separate solar water heating systems, and a safe, hygienic environment. Additionally, an emergency vehicle facility is available to assist students in case of medical needs or emergencies. `n `n `n Does the campus provide Wi-Fi? `n Yes, internet facilities are available on campus. `n `n `n Where is MITCORER located? `n MITCORER is located in Industrial Estate No. 03 - Barshi, Dist. Solapur, Maharashtra (India) - 413401. `n `n `n How can I contact the college? `n You can contact through phone (91 84599 67882, +91 86696 62106), Email: info.mitcorer@mitpune.edu.in, or the official website: https://www.mitcorer.edu.in `n `n `n Are scholarships available? `n Yes, government scholarships and financial aid schemes are available for eligible students. `n `n `n Why should I choose MITCORER? `n MITCORER offers industry-oriented education, experienced faculty, modern infrastructure, and a unique specialization in Railway Engineering. `n `n `n Is MITCORER Barshi the same as MIT Pune? `n Yes, both MITCORER Barshi and MIT Pune are part of the same parent organization, the MAEER’s MIT Group of Institutions, Pune. MITCORER (Barshi campus) has been established under this group with the objective of providing quality technical education to rural students and creating opportunities for their academic and professional growth. While both campuses operate under the same management, they function as separate institutions with their own infrastructure, courses, and campus facilities. `n `n `n How does MITCORER ensure quality in teaching and learning? `n The institute adopts modern teaching methodologies, including ICT-enabled learning, practical sessions, project-based learning, and continuous internal assessment to ensure effective knowledge delivery. `n `n `n Does the institute follow outcome-based education (OBE)? `n Yes, MITCORER follows Outcome-Based Education (OBE), focusing on Program Outcomes (POs), Program Specific Outcomes (PSOs), and Course Outcomes (COs) to enhance student learning and performance. Additionally, the institute follows the curriculum framework of Punyashlok Ahilyadevi Holkar Solapur University (PAHSUS), Solapur, which is aligned with the NEP 2020 (National Education Policy 2020) pattern and scheme, ensuring holistic, multidisciplinary, and skill-oriented education. `n `n `n Are industry-oriented programs included in the curriculum? `n Yes, the curriculum is designed to include industry-oriented training, workshops, seminars, and skill development programs to enhance employability. `n `n `n `n `n `n `n `n

These representatives will be responsible for operationalizing the Placement Process. At the commencement of each academic year, each department will constitute a Placement Committee consisting of representatives from faculty (1), and students (3) to be nominated by the HOD of respective department.`n The Placement Office will facilitate the placement of all eligible students who are validly enrolled in the respective programmes. All students who are eligible and require placement assistance must fill a Placement Registration Form.`n `n Mandatory: Once registered, each student must participate in all placement activities. Students wishing to opt out of the placement assistance can do so by signing the declaration in Appendix 1. `n `n 01`n Campus placement involves interacting with external entities. It represents a significant opportunity for creating goodwill and esteem for the student and institute. Students are cautioned to display civility and good professional conduct while interacting with external entities.`n `n 02`n If any student is found to be in violation of professional code of conduct, he/she is liable to be debarred from placement assistance.`n `n 03`n All participating students are required to be present in the institute on all days of placement-related activities in formal attires. For male students this means college uniform with formal black/brown shoes.`n `n 04`n It is the student's responsibility to follow all deadlines arising out of the placement processes. Students must regularly check emails, messages, or notices from the online portal. Non-adherence to timelines may lead to denial of subsequent process outcomes such as interviews.`n `n 05`n If a student eligible as per the Job Description chooses not to apply for three (3) consecutive eligible job postings, it may validly imply that the student is not interested. In such cases, the student will be denied further placement assistance.`n `n 06`n The Institute follows a one student, one job offer policy . It becomes mandatory for the student to accept the first job offer. Upon receiving the first job offer, the student will be automatically considered as placed and removed from the list of students awaiting job offers. `n `n 07`n Students are expected to behave professionally with all employees of the institute. Any misconduct, misbehavior, or non-maintenance of decorum would be dealt with seriously and could lead to disqualification from all placement-related assistance.`n `n `n `n `n Section 2 Eligibility`n `n `n The institute would facilitate final placement of its students undergoing UG Programme basis fulfilling the below mentioned criteria.`n 01`n Successfully completed the semester examinations/course with aCGPA equivalent to 6 or higher , and with no backlogs. (The criteria may vary from recruiter and will be shared with students for every drive.) `n `n 02`n Satisfactory conduct with no disciplinary action throughout the program.`n `n 03`n Good attendance record in their courses and has good participation in Placement Activities (Guest Lectures / Seminars / Conferences / Industry Visits etc.).`n `n 04`n 90% attendance in the proposed trainings conducted as part of training and development activity by TNP Cell.`n `n 05`n Graduating students who wish to pursue their startup ambitions instead of seeking placements, may seek deferment from the on-campus placement process by obtaining formal approvals from their respective HOD, TPO and final approval from Principal by 1st week of the applicable academic year.`n `n `n `n `n Section 3 Placement Process`n `n `n The institute will follow a rolling placement process starting July/August every year. The placement process will have the flexibility to accommodate the needs of recruiting organizations. `n 01`n Recruiting companies will inform the institute about their requirements, role descriptions, eligibility norms and the remuneration packages being offered.`n `n 02`n These details will be shared with students through the Placement Committee and placement portal. Students will be able to decide about participating depending upon their interest, suitability, specializations and career interests.`n `n 03`n Resumes along with academic details of interested and/or suitable students will be sent to the recruiting organization, basis which the company will notify a shortlist of students.`n `n 04`n Shortlisted students will be informed about the selection process which may include: Personal or online Assessment, Telephonic interview, Case Discussion, Group Discussion, Multiple rounds of Interviews — conducted on campus or at other premises.`n `n 05`n Students may be required to go to the company's office or pool campus locations for final placements as decided by the company.`n `n `n `n `n Section 4 Early Joining`n `n `n Companies may indicate early joining in their offer letters. Such cases will be reported to the Placement Office, HOD and Dean.`n At present, the Institute does not have an explicit policy for early joining. However, such early joining may be permitted depending on the merits of the case.`n `n In all circumstances, the student would be allowed to join early only if recommended by the respective HOD and approved by the Principal.`n `n If a student is allowed to join early, he/she would have to give an undertaking to diligently undertake the Assignments given and report to the concerned faculty member on mutually agreed days.`n `n Failure in submitting the assignments and meeting faculty members on the assigned day(s) may result in withholding of the degree.`n `n The student must manage the leave of absence from the company, to write their final examinations and complete other academic requirements in time.`n `n `n `n `n Section 5 Corporate Readiness Program`n `n `n MIT CORER TNP CELL Corporate Readiness Program is designed in a manner to help you make the best out of every market situation and achieve a good start in your career. As Trustee & Secretary General of MAEER's MIT Group of Institutions, she believes that education should not only create skilled professionals, but also responsible citizens capable of shaping the future.`n With a strong focus on emerging infrastructure and technological advancement, she emphasizes the importance of specialized education in sectors like Railway Engineering—an area crucial to India's economic growth and national development.`n Driven by the philosophy of value-based learning, she envisions institutions that nurture students through:`n 01 Innovation-driven education`n 02 Critical thinking & practical learning`n 03 Industry-oriented skill development`n 04 Holistic personality growth`n `n Educational Vision & Philosophy`n Prof. Swati Karad Chate believes that true education combines technical expertise with ethics, creativity, and lifelong learning. Timeless Values.`n Heartiest Greetings from the team of MIT College of Railway Engineering and Research (MITCORER), Barshi. It gives me immense pleasure to introduce us as the only engineering institute in India offering Bachelor in Engineering (B.E.) in Railway Engineering. With the vision of the Founder and Executive President of MAEER, Prof. Dr. Vishwanath D. Karad, MITCORER has launched the first-of-its-kind engineering institute in India, which offers a promising career in the field of railway and high speed transportation systems, based on artificial intelligence.`n Courses and value-added trainings in these unique areas are available throughout the world and offer promising career over and above other branches of engineering. In India, railways being the biggest employer in the country with its vast network and with the vision of Bullet Train and futuristic Hyper Loop mode of transportation, the degree of B.E. in Railway Engineering will get increased attention. The sector needs qualified and skilled manpower to deliver with expertise and render services in India and abroad. To support the curriculum of Railway Engineering, MITCORER has offered four other engineering branches, viz. Civil, Mechanical, Computer Science and Electronics and Telecommunication, as an interdisciplinary approach to serve the railway sector.`n Aspiring students can have dual advantage of employment in railway or other sectors like infrastructure, construction, machinery, chemical, IT, satellite and radio technologies, mobile computing, automobile and many more. With the upcoming Railway University in India, MITCORER shall have an extra advantage over other engineering institutions to offer expertise and consultancy services in the 21st century futuristic engineering and technology to support high speed transportation systems to be a part of the Smart Cities initiative. We are taking forward the legacy of MIT Group of Institutions with the unique project called MITCORER.`n I welcome the aspiring candidates to pursue engineering career at a premier institute like MITCORER. The cell is actively addressing society's technical and non-technical demands by crafting impactful proposals and securing sanctions from reputed government agencies.`n Our R&D Cell has several ongoing research proposals in the pipeline under esteemed government schemes such as ANRF, MSME and industry collaborations. These initiatives reflect our commitment to contributing to national and societal growth through meaningful research and innovation.`n In addition to driving research, the R&D Cell regularly organizes Faculty Development Programs (FDPs) and webinars to foster a robust research culture among the faculty. The cell also motivates faculty members from various disciplines to attend sessions on Intellectual Property Rights (IPR) and research methodologies at external institutes, enhancing their expertise and broadening their horizons.`n To further encourage academic excellence, the R&D Cell offers incentives for publishing research papers, filing patents, and participating in prestigious conferences across India and internationally.
